name: DynaTex
description: Dataset distillation aims to synthesize a tiny set of images that can train neural networks nearly as effectively as the full dataset. Recent trajectory matching methods have achieved remarkable progress by aligning the optimization paths of student networks trained on synthetic data with expert trajectories trained on real data. However, they are still challenged by unstable long-horizon matching, ineffective utilization of limited synthetic samples, and a lack of semantic structure in distilled data. We propose DynaTex, a dynamic and semantically enhanced trajectory-based distillation framework. DynaTex introduces (1) difficulty-aligned trajectory matching that adaptively selects teacher stages according to the IPC budget, (2) per-iteration online top-K selection that dynamically prioritizes the most informative synthetic samples via instantaneous gradient norms, and (3) textual soft labels derived from frozen CLIP text embeddings to inject rich semantic priors. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100 and TinyImageNet demonstrate that DynaTex significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods and, under multiple settings, achieves near-lossless performance compared to training on the entire real dataset.
